front.title: AI Automation and AI Agents for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: AI agents and business automation for founder-led DTC brands, with clear inputs, human review and useful reporting.
front.lead: Give repeat work a reliable system.

steps.title: Map the work
steps.text: Find the repeated steps in lead handling, reporting and operations. Define the inputs, permissions and result before building.

steps.title: Connect the systems
steps.text: Build workflows and agents around the tools the business uses. Keep approval steps where a mistake could affect a customer or a live account.

steps.title: Watch the exceptions
steps.text: Log what ran, surface failures and make the next action clear. A system needs maintenance and review after it is switched on.

faqs.q: Where should we use AI first?
faqs.a: Start with a repeated task whose inputs and result are clear. The roadmap helps decide whether it needs AI or a simpler automation.

faqs.q: Will everything run without review?
faqs.a: No. The review steps depend on the task, the data and what a mistake could change.

faqs.q: How do you price an automation project?
faqs.a: We scope it after the roadmap, based on the workflow, integrations and ongoing support.

ai-automation.body: A useful automation has a defined job, a way to check its work and a person who owns the exceptions. We start with the process before choosing tools.

front.title: Email Marketing Automation for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Retention and email systems for DTC brands, connecting lifecycle messages, customer behavior and store results.
front.lead: Keep the conversation going after the first order.

steps.title: Review the customer journey
steps.text: Look at signup, welcome, abandoned checkout, post-purchase and returning-customer paths. Check consent, suppression and overlapping messages.

steps.title: Make each message useful
steps.text: Connect flows and campaigns to what a customer did and what they need next. Keep the offer, timing and destination aligned.

steps.title: Measure with context
steps.text: Read attributed revenue alongside order data, deliverability and customer behavior. An email platform claim alone does not establish incremental sales.

faqs.q: Can you work with our existing email setup?
faqs.a: Yes. We review the current platform, flows and data before deciding what to change.

faqs.q: Is this only about sending more campaigns?
faqs.a: No. The work may start with missing flows, message overlap, data quality or the experience after purchase.

faqs.q: What will retention work cost?
faqs.a: The scope follows the roadmap and depends on the flows, campaigns and technical work needed.

email-marketing-automation.body: The first purchase is the start of a customer relationship. We review the messages and timing around it to find where useful follow-up is missing.

front.title: Google Ads Management for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Google Ads management for DTC brands, with search intent, product feeds and store results considered together.
front.lead: Meet buyers who are already looking.

steps.title: Check what brings customers
steps.text: Review search terms, branded and nonbranded traffic, conversion setup and the products receiving budget.

steps.title: Match the campaign to the store
steps.text: Organize search and shopping work around the catalog, buying intent and landing pages. Check product information before treating a feed issue as an ad issue.

steps.title: Make the next decision clear
steps.text: Explain what changed, what the data can support and which test comes next. Keep budget decisions tied to business results.

faqs.q: Can you review an existing Google Ads account?
faqs.a: Yes. We can start with the current account and identify what needs to be kept, repaired or tested.

faqs.q: Do you work on product feeds?
faqs.a: Product information and feed issues are part of the review when shopping campaigns depend on them.

faqs.q: How is the work priced?
faqs.a: We scope the work after the roadmap, based on the account and the problems to solve.

google-ads-management.body: A search click carries a question. Your campaign, product page and offer should answer the same one. We review that path before recommending more spend.

front.title: Creator and Affiliate Programs for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Creator and affiliate program systems for founder-led DTC brands, including onboarding, links, follow-up and performance tracking.
front.lead: Build a program you can track and maintain.

steps.title: Define the program
steps.text: Set the partner fit, product story, approved claims and terms before outreach. Identify who owns each approval.

steps.title: Organize the work
steps.text: Create a process for onboarding, links, codes, assets and follow-up. Keep partners and internal teams working from the same information.

steps.title: Review the results
steps.text: Connect partner activity to tracked orders where the data allows. Explain attribution gaps and distinguish content delivery from sales performance.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee creator sales?
faqs.a: No. Results depend on the offer, audience, execution and measurement. We define the test and review what the evidence shows.

faqs.q: Can you improve a program we already have?
faqs.a: Yes. We can review its onboarding, tracking and follow-up process before proposing changes.

faqs.q: How is a program scoped?
faqs.a: The roadmap identifies the setup and support needed. Commercial terms are agreed separately before the work starts.

influencer-affiliate.body: A creator program needs more than a list of names. It needs a clear offer, a repeatable way to work with partners and a useful record of what happens.

front.title: Meta Ads Management for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Meta ads for founder-led DTC brands, connecting campaign decisions to acquisition costs, landing pages and repeat purchases.
front.lead: Give every ad a clear job.

steps.title: Find the constraint
steps.text: Review account structure, customer acquisition costs and the route from ad to checkout. Separate a campaign problem from an offer or page problem.

steps.title: Build a useful testing plan
steps.text: Set up campaigns around clear hypotheses. Compare messages and audiences with agreed spending limits and enough context to interpret results.

steps.title: Read beyond the platform
steps.text: Review platform results alongside store sales and customer data. A reported return on ad spend is one input, not a profit statement.

faqs.q: Do we need a bigger ad budget?
faqs.a: We start with the data you have. The roadmap may call for changes to the offer, page or measurement before more spending.

faqs.q: Do you handle the landing page too?
faqs.a: Landing pages and conversion work can be part of the plan when the path after the ad needs attention.

faqs.q: What does the work cost?
faqs.a: The scope comes after the roadmap, based on the work your numbers need.

meta-ads.body: More spend only helps when the offer, creative and store can turn attention into customers. We look at those pieces together before deciding what to change.

front.title: SEO and AEO Services for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Search engine and answer engine optimization for DTC brands, built around useful content, technical foundations and clear product information.
front.lead: Answer the questions buyers bring to search.

steps.title: Check the foundations
steps.text: Review indexing, page structure, internal links and structured data. Make sure important product and category pages can be found.

steps.title: Write useful answers
steps.text: Connect buyer questions to clear page content. Use accurate product information and relevant proof, with claims reviewed before publication.

steps.title: Track discovery and action
steps.text: Review search visibility alongside visits and useful store actions. Treat AI answer visibility as something to observe, not a placement we can promise.

faqs.q: What is AEO?
faqs.a: Answer engine optimization is the work of making accurate, useful information easier for answer systems to interpret and cite.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee rankings or AI citations?
faqs.a: No. We can improve the content and technical foundations, but search engines and answer systems decide what they show.

faqs.q: Do you sell a fixed SEO package?
faqs.a: The scope comes after the roadmap and reflects the site, content and technical work needed.

seo.body: Your pages should be easy for people to understand and for search systems to read. We work on the technical and content gaps that get in the way.

front.title: Social Media Management for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Organic social systems for DTC brands, with planning, approvals, publishing and reporting connected in one process.
front.lead: Give useful content a repeatable path to publication.

steps.title: Set the working plan
steps.text: Define the audience, topics, approved claims and available material. Match the publishing plan to what the team can support.

steps.title: Connect review and publishing
steps.text: Make briefs, feedback and approvals easy to follow. Build a repeatable schedule with a clear owner for each step.

steps.title: Learn from the response
steps.text: Review reach, engagement and useful site actions together. Feed the findings into the next plan without treating every interaction as a sale.

faqs.q: Is this a standalone creative studio service?
faqs.a: The focus is the publishing and operating system. Creative needs are assessed as part of the broader plan and available material.

faqs.q: Can we keep reviewing posts before they go out?
faqs.a: Yes. The approval process is agreed before publishing and should reflect the brand and its claims requirements.

faqs.q: What does social support cost?
faqs.a: We scope the work after the roadmap, based on the channels, material, workflow and support needed.

social-media-management.body: Consistent publishing depends on more than ideas. We help organize the work from approved source material to posts, review and reporting.

front.title: Landing Page Design and CRO for DTC Brands | Freeland
front.description: Landing pages and conversion rate optimization for founder-led DTC brands, from the ad promise to the product page and checkout.
front.lead: Make the next step easier to take.

steps.title: Understand the buying path
steps.text: Review the ad promise, mobile page, product details and checkout route. Check whether key events tell you what customers actually do.

steps.title: Build around one decision
steps.text: Give the page a clear offer, useful proof, direct answers and a next step. Keep content readable and usable on a phone.

steps.title: Test the change
steps.text: Agree on the measure before launch. Compare outcomes with enough context to avoid confusing a promotion or traffic shift with a page improvement.

faqs.q: Do we need a full website rebuild?
faqs.a: Not always. A focused page or checkout-path improvement may be the better starting point.

faqs.q: What does CRO mean?
faqs.a: Conversion rate optimization means finding and testing changes that help more visitors complete a useful action, such as buying.

faqs.q: Can you quote the project now?
faqs.a: We scope the work after the roadmap so the quote reflects the pages and problems that need attention.

website-design.body: The page should help a buyer understand the offer, trust the business and take the next step. We focus the work on the points where that decision gets difficult.
